description: We are a passionate group of students, developers, and designers united by curiosity about space and a desire to solve real-world problems using NASA’s open data. Our team combines technical skills, creativity, and teamwork to build an innovative solution for this year’s challenge while learning from each other along the way.
summary:
AstroHealth is a browser-based health-monitoring prototype designed around the challenges of astronaut missions. It brings several workflows into one place: a Self-Check for entering symptoms and mission context; a Health Map for exploring body systems and explicitly linked information; file-based ECG beat and sleep-stage analysis; and tools for wellbeing check-ins, mission environment, reminders, and emergency guidance. The models provide experimental rankings or classifications based on the submitted inputs. Health entries and check-ins are saved in the browser. The current prototype accepts files rather than connecting directly to a wearable. 
In space, crew members may need to review health information in a demanding, remote environment. AstroHealth aims to make that information easier to collect and explore by bringing symptoms, measurements, sensor-file results, and body-system context together. We hope it can support crew awareness and clearer conversations with medical or mission support. It is a prototype—not a diagnostic tool or a replacement for mission-approved procedures.
